items.title: Dolly Parton, One of Country Music’s Biggest & Brightest Icons, Dies at 80
items.summary: Parton was one of the most influential songwriters to hit Nashville -- or the world
items.body: Dolly Parton , the extraordinarily versatile singer and songwriter who built up her artistic credibility and commercial fortunes in both country and pop music over more than half a century, died in Nashville on Tuesday (Aug. 25) at the age of 80. Parton had been mostly out of sight eye for the past year following a struggle with unspecified health issues that forced the “9 to 5” singer/songwriter to curtail public appearances and postpone, then cancel her planned 2025 Las Vegas residency. Her death came 17 months after the passing of her husband of nearly 60 years, Carl Dean, who died on March 3, 2025 at age 82. “At Dolly’s request, a small, private service will be held for immediate family,” read a press release announcing the awful news. “Dolly’s fans and friends from around the world are encouraged to pay tribute to Dolly on social media by tagging @DollyParton or by leaving a message at www.dollyparton.com. In lieu of flowers the family asks for donations to be made to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library at www.imaginationlibrary.com.” Her nephew, Bryan Seaver, shared a message on Instagram after her passing. items.body: TL;DR Newly leaked images show that Philips Hue could soon release an adapter to integrate Nanoleaf Shapes lights. Back in June, a Philips Hue user spotted that the app had added a new light type icon for hexagonal panel lights that looks more than a little like lights offered by Nanoleaf. At the time, we assumed that meant that Hue was cooking up its own hexagonal panel lights — but now, it looks like the icon may actually have been Nanoleaf lights, after all. Smartlights.de has shared some information about an unannounced “wall light module” from Philips Hue. The report says that Hue will release a kind of adapter for Nanoleaf’s Shapes lights that’ll let users integrate the third-party wall lights into existing Hue setups.

Reaching the state of serenity isn’t just by happenstance, but the aftermath of resilience. items.title: Forever No. 1: Shelley Fabares, ‘Johnny Angel’

items.body: Forever No. 1 is a Billboard series that pays special tribute to the recently deceased artists who achieved the highest honor our charts have to offer — a Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 single — by taking an extended look back at the chart-topping songs that made them part of this exclusive club. Here, we honor the late TV star Shelley Fabares, whose “Johnny Angel” reached No. 1 in April 1962. “Johnny Angel” is so innocent, so chaste, that it immediately conjures a simpler time. items.title: Frustrating Google Home bug refuses to add items to your shopping lists in Keep
items.summary: Another day, another Google Home bug.
items.body: TL;DR Some Google Home users are facing a bug where the voice assistant refuses to add items to their Google Keep lists. While not all users appear to be facing this issue, it appears widespread enough for Google to take notice. Meanwhile, a quick look at Google Home settings suggests that access to notes & lists using a voice assistant may have been removed. It feels like we’re reporting on a Google Home bug or a fix almost every other day. Only today, users received some good news following reports of devices refusing to set alarms over voice commands. Sadly, those good times aren’t going to last, and it now looks like yet another function is being impacted by a similar glitch, as some people are seemingly unable to add items to their lists on Google Keep using Google Home voice commands. In a series of complaints on Reddit, including one from Friday, a user claims the voice assistant recognizes their commands perfectly well, but refuses to add items to the list . For instance, if the person asks one of their Google Home devices to “add x to list xyz,” the assistant might respond by saying how many items are on that list, while refusing to add any new items.

Google didn’t share any dollar figures or specifics on the types of in-app purchases foldable owners are making. Foldable phones cost a lot more than non-folding ones — the Pixel 11 Pro Fold starts at $1,900 to the regular 11 Pro’s $1,100 — so it stands to reason that many of the customers buying them are in the habit of spending generously on their mobile experience. A recent post on the official Android Developers X account claims that foldable owners aren’t just spending more on hardware, but also an order of magnitude more on the software they’re downloading, too. The post Android Developers shared makes the claim that foldable users spend a whopping 14 times more on purchases within apps than users with non-folding phones. items.body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Earlier this year, Google gave Gemini the ability to generate interactive simulations and models. This feature is now rolling out to all Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users who meet the minimum age requirements. The update is available now in the Gemini app. If you’re having trouble understanding a complicated subject, sometimes visualization can do the trick. However, while an image can be helpful, having a visual model that you can actually interact with is even better. As Gemini is a tool that’s commonly used to help people understand complex concepts, it’s only natural that Gemini is gaining the ability to generate simulations and models. If this sounds familiar, it’s because Google announced the same feature back in April. However, Google says it is now rolling the feature out for Workspace users. This includes Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users who meet the minimum age requirements.

items.title: Poll shows plenty of Pixel 10 Pro owners are skipping the Pixel 11 Pro
items.summary: Annual upgrades continue to lose their shine, even for Pixel owners.
items.body: It’s certainly tempting to upgrade the moment your smartphone’s successor is released. It’s a feeling that many Pixel 10 and older owners likely felt and are still feeling this week, given that the Pixel 11 series is now available. However, as strong as that temptation might be, it’s often far smarter to resist it. This rings true for Pixel 10 Pro owners in particular, a phone that still has plenty going for it. A little over a year into its lifespan, it can look forward to some six years of software support; its cameras remain some of the best in the game; and it likely won’t slow to a crawl in any noticeable way in the coming months or years.

items.title: Super Smash Bros. is ready for its unofficial Android port
items.summary: You can't play it on Switch, but unsanctioned Android ports could be coming soon.
items.body: TL;DR Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 64 has been fully decompiled, opening the door to unofficial native ports. The 1999 platform fighter hasn’t been available through official means for several years and isn’t currently playable on Nintendo Switch consoles. We aren’t aware of any ports made from the newly decompiled code yet, but we expect they’ll start appearing soon. Aside from some high-profile rereleases, present-day Nintendo is notoriously stingy when it comes to providing easy, legitimate access to its immense back catalog of classic games. This, in part, has inspired fans to take matters into their own hands by decompiling old favorites, recreating their source code so the games can be easily (if unofficially) ported to modern platforms like Windows or Android. Now, another classic that’s been inaccessible on modern hardware is ripe for porting: 1999’s Super Smash Bros. has been fully decompiled. As shared on Decomp.dev , Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 64 is now “100.00% decompiled,” meaning the game’s source code has been completely recreated and it’s ready to be ported. Google has already built deep integrations for its core apps like Google Maps, Photos, Gboard, and the Play Store. Last year, we uncovered development on Live Translate for Google’s extended reality platform. We can now exclusively reveal a potential feature addition for the Live Translate experience on Android XR. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. items.summary: New leaked images offer a closer look at Xiaomi’s mysterious wide-screen foldable.
items.body: TL;DR Xiaomi’s next foldable has leaked, showing a wide inner display and a design that closely resembles the company’s own HyperOS 4 teaser. The Xiaomi 18 Fold launches in September, but key details such as global availability, pricing, and dimensions remain unknown. Xiaomi’s XRing O3 chipset has already made headlines with some seriously ambitious performance claims, but the chip’s first phone may be just as interesting. Xiaomi has confirmed that the 3nm processor will debut in the Xiaomi 18 Fold next month, and now leaked images appear to show the company’s upcoming foldable in the flesh. The images, which Digital Chat Station (DCS) shared on Weibo , show a book-style foldable with a wide inner display similar to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 , relatively thick bezels, and a punch-hole selfie camera near the upper-right corner. One image also shows the rear of the device, including a large camera module, but it doesn’t reveal enough to say much about its hardware.

items.title: Nothing unveils Nothing OS 5.0 built on Android 17, but there’s bad news for older phones
items.summary: Older phones will not be receiving this update, as expected.
items.body: TL;DR Nothing has announced Nothing OS 5.0, bringing a massive overhaul featuring the Geist typeface, translucent software layering, dynamic wallpaper-tinted adaptive themes, and dedicated apps for both the Glyph Interface and Essential Apps Builder. The update also introduces Android 17 platform features such as split notification and Quick Settings panels, cross-platform Quick Share with iOS, enhanced privacy indicators, and more. Open Beta testing for the Nothing Phone 3 starts tomorrow, with a full stable release expected in mid-October. However, Phone 1, Phone 2, and CMF Phone 1 will not receive the update. Nothing has officially revealed Nothing OS 5.0, detailing the next major evolution of its custom Android skin. Built on top of Android 17 , the platform update brings a visual design overhaul, expanded lock screen personalization, new first-party widgets, and tighter system-level integration with the Glyph Interface. Following an announcement teased on X , Nothing published a detailed breakdown of the new features and the design evolution on its community forums.

items.title: The next flagship Snapdragon will be the first 5GHz smartphone chip, and here’s why you should care
items.summary: Thought today's smartphone CPUs had high clock speeds? Qualcomm will make a giant leap forward next month.
items.body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority TL;DR Qualcomm has announced the first details for its next-generation Snapdragon flagship processor. The new processor has a 5GHz CPU, making it the first smartphone CPU to reach this milestone. A new “FlexCache” architecture also delivers more performance improvements. Qualcomm has teased the arrival of two Snapdragon 8 Elite series chips at its Snapdragon Summit next month. Now, the company has revealed the first details about its new silicon, and it might have an impressive CPU. Qualcomm has officially detailed the CPU for its next-generation Snapdragon processor, and this is the first smartphone CPU to reach 5GHz. That’s an impressive achievement on paper and comes after the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy reached a peak speed of 4.74GHz. The firm’s own graphic shows that you can expect two 5GHz CPU cores along with six “performance” cores running at an unspecified frequency.

items.body: TL;DR According to a new leak, Qualcomm’s next flagship chip will be called the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. It could feature two prime cores clocked at 5.01GHz, along with three performance and three efficiency cores. The Dimensity 9600 Pro could also use two prime cores clocked at 4.55GHz, along with three performance and three efficiency cores. Qualcomm and MediaTek are both gearing up to launch their latest flagship processors. The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series and the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro are expected to feature improvements across the board. Now, a new leak is shedding some light on the core arrangement and clock speeds of the top-of-the-line Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and the Dimensity 9600 Pro. According to a Weibo post by Digital Chat Station (DCS), the upcoming Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro, model number SM8975, could be called the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 instead. The extremely long (pun intended) and unnecessarily weird name notwithstanding, Qualcomm’s next flagship chip seems set to break the 5GHz barrier for smartphone chipsets.

items.title: Galaxy S26 series gets sixth One UI 9 beta release, but when is the stable update coming?
items.summary: The latest 851MB update targets several UI and routine issues for global users ahead of the stable launch.
items.body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has released the sixth One UI 9 beta for the Galaxy S26 series. The 851MB update (firmware ZZHE) includes the August 5, 2026, security patch and fixes key issues, including display errors with the Now Brief widget and photo-saving issues in Expert RAW 24MP at specific focal lengths. Currently live in Germany, India, Poland, the UK, and South Korea, the new update will soon be available in the US as well. Samsung entered One UI 9 development with much gusto, but after releasing the stable update alongside the new Galaxy Z8 foldables, the pace of One UI 9 beta releases for its previous flagships has slowed down a bit. After releasing the fifth One UI 9 beta almost two weeks ago, Samsung is now picking things up with the sixth One UI 9 beta release for the Galaxy S26 series. We’ve received the sixth One UI 9 update on our Galaxy S26 Ultra in the UK. This Android 17-based update comes with firmware version ending in ZZHE, the August 5, 2026 security patch, and is 851MB in size.

items.title: 5 reasons I may not go back to Spotify after trying YouTube Music
items.summary: YouTube Music isn't perfect, but you can't ignore the value proposition.
items.body: As is the case with millions of users around the world, I’ve been a loyal Spotify subscriber for as long as I can remember. The app works well across Android and iOS, there’s a great selection of music, and features like Jam and Spotify Connect have made my listening experience much more seamless across audio devices at home. I was happy to pay for the Premium Duo plan — until it was sneakily taken away. Spotify removed the Duo plan in India around November 2025, but as I had subscribed to it long before, I was able to continue with it, as it should be. Then came the email, one July morning this year, saying my Premium Duo plan was canceled due to an “issue” with my payment method. Nothing had changed, so it didn’t make any sense. I figured it was Spotify forcing me to upgrade to a higher-priced plan, and as it turned out, I wasn’t the only one who got the boot. Frustrated with this move, I decided to try other options.

items.title: Google Home made users say the weirdest thing to set an alarm, but that’s over now
items.summary: It's a small fix, but a welcome one for anyone who relies on voice alarms daily.
items.body: TL;DR Some Google Home devices stopped setting alarms via voice command for several days. The bug hit both Google Assistant and Gemini for Home, affecting Nest speakers, displays, and even third-party devices like Lenovo smart displays. Google has confirmed the fix, and our own testing shows alarms are setting and triggering correctly again. Google Home has had a busy August, with Google rolling out several updates that make Gemini for Home smarter and add new capabilities to its smart home platform. But amid all those improvements, something as basic as setting an alarm suddenly stopped working for some users. Thankfully, Google has now confirmed that the issue affecting Nest and other Gemini-powered smart home devices has been fixed. For several days, users on Reddit reported that commands such as “Hey Google, set an alarm for 8:30 AM” would simply be ignored. Some found that alarms worked when set for an exact hour, while others had to ask Google to set an alarm first and then provide the time when prompted. One odd workaround involved saying “Hey Google, hi” before giving the alarm command.

items.title: The Pixel 11 Pro’s camera flash is a ‘LoLight’ thanks to HiLight
items.summary: Users complain that the Pixel 11 Pro's camera flash is a big downgrade over other phones, and HiLight could be to blame here.
items.body: Credit: Sanuj Bhatia / Android Authority TL;DR Reddit users report that the Google Pixel 11 Pro’s camera flash is significantly weaker than that of older Pixels and competitors. Our preliminary testing here at Android Authority shows the Pixel 11 Pro XL torch mode registered 89 lux compared to 123 lux on the Pixel 10 Pro XL. The physical diffuser added to the camera visor for the new HiLight LED array is likely the cause of the softer beam. Google’s new Pixel 11 Pro series introduces HiLight , a small array of ambient LEDs around the camera flash that give you some bits of information without requiring you to turn over or unlock your phone. Google ended up severely limiting HiLight’s functionality, and users had to resort to apps like HiLight Studio to unlock the LED’s full potential. As it turns out, Google gimped HiLight in more ways than one, with the LED flash itself also downgraded compared to the Pixel 10 series. Reddit user pcman2000 voiced their frustration with the Pixel 11 Pro’s camera flash, calling it “really weak” and the weakest among all the phones they tested, ranking it below the Pixel 9 Pro and even the iPhone 17e.

items.title: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a camera problem, and it has nothing to do with photo quality
items.summary: Samsung put the Galaxy Z Fold 8's folding display selfie camera in the worst spot.
items.body: I’ve spent years trying the latest book-style foldables, but none earned a permanent spot in my pocket once I finished testing them. Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 7 came the closest with a thin-and-light design and truly flagship specs. Unfortunately, it suffered from the same problems as every other folding phone with a squarish inner screen aspect ratio. The form factor isn’t conducive to widescreen video content, as you’ll see large black bars at the top and bottom of the folding screen. Samsung built the wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 to specifically address this pain point, and it quickly won me over. Then, something happened that I didn’t expect. I found myself using the Galaxy Z Fold 8 unfolded in portrait orientation more than landscape.

items.title: We tried Gemini’s new Device Help feature on the Pixel 11, and the results were mixed
items.summary: Gemini is ready to fix your Pixel, well, almost ready.
items.body: TL;DR Gemini’s experimental Device Help feature is appearing in the Gemini app on Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro devices, letting you troubleshoot your phone using natural language. It can diagnose battery and Wi-Fi issues, open specific settings, change things like brightness and dark mode, and explain Pixel features without making you hunt through Settings. It’s still a Labs feature and can get things wrong. Our testing produced inconsistent instructions for Magic Capture, so it isn’t completely reliable yet. A few days ago, we spotted Google testing a clever new Gemini trick that could save Pixel users from digging through the Settings app every time something goes wrong. That feature, called Device Help, is now appearing directly inside the Gemini app on some of our Pixel 11 series devices. First spotted by 9to5Google , Device Help is currently showing up on Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro models we’ve checked, including our Pixel 11 Pro XL units. Unfortunately, this also made it harder to install extensions like the highly popular uBlock Origin. While workarounds still existed by using Chrome flags, that’s no longer the case . It is now virtually impossible to get MV2 extensions to work in Chrome.

items.title: Nintendo just went nuclear on Switch emulators (again)

items.body: TL;DR Nintendo has filed seven new DMCA notices taking down over 400 GitHub repositories related to Switch emulators. The notice took down repos for emulators such as Suyu, Skyline, and several others. It’s no secret that Nintendo has historically taken an extremely strict stance against emulators and people using its IP without permission. A few months ago, the company sent DMCA notices to take down several Switch emulators whose code was hosted on GitHub. Now, the company has thrown another proverbial Donkey Kong barrel at more such GitHub repositories. Nintendo has filed seven DMCA complaints with GitHub to take down over 400 repositories related to Switch emulators in a single day (via TorrentFreak ). This includes emulators like Suyu, which gained popularity after the Yuzu emulator shut down in 2024. According to the DMCA notice displayed publicly on the Suyu repository, GitHub took down all 311 repositories in the network due to Nintendo’s DMCA notice.

items.body: TL;DR Google’s Android Pulse app is starting to appear as an available update in the Play Store. The background service appears to detect unusual resource usage, such as apps suddenly consuming too much battery, memory, or processing power. Android Pulse isn’t new; builds date back to March, and the Play Store shows more than 10 million downloads. There are plenty of Google apps you probably use every day, but Android Pulse is definitely not one of them. In fact, you may not even know it exists. That could change soon, though, because this mysterious system app is suddenly showing up as an available update in the Play Store. Its job appears to be pretty simple: keep an eye out for apps or parts of Android that are using your phone’s resources in unusual ways.

items.summary: في اكتشاف علمي يحقق توقعا طرحه عالم الطبيعة البريطاني تشارلز داروين قبل نحو 150 عاما، أعلن باحثون أن نباتا جبليا ينمو في الصين، كان يعتقد لسنوات طويلة أنه نبات مزهر عادي، هو في الواقع نبات لاحم يصطاد الحشرات ويهضمها للحصول على العناصر الغذائية.

items.title: مصر.. تحرك عاجل لوقف فعالية طبيبة أسترالية مثيرة للجدل
items.summary: أطلقت نقابة الأطباء المصرية تحركا رسميا لوقف فعالية صحية كان من المقرر أن تشارك فيها طبيبة أسترالية بمدينة الجونة، بعدما أكدت أنها "ممنوعة مدى الحياة من تقديم أي خدمات أو نصائح صحية"، محذرة من أن الأفكار التي تروج لها تتعارض مع الأدلة العلمية المعتمدة، وتشكل خطرا على صحة المواطنين.
